findings.title: The new goal keyword (and target_name) is a bridge-supplied planner input that no gate pins
findings.problem: v4 introduces main(goal=...) as the way D7's conjunctive goal reaches the planner, and keeps target_name as an injected keyword. main() passes whatever goal it receives to every planner.plan() call. No gate checks it: G10 checks planner and streams types and the domain and stream hashes, G11 checks the solve call path, the call count and list identity, G7 greps scene literals, G3 compares executed steps with the plan that came back. A bridge that supplies one extra conjunct, for example an obj_at_boxel fluent for a cup symbol obtained from the identity table (no literal such as cup_0 appears, so G7 stays green) and a free boxel, makes the planner relocate that cup to that place: WHAT and WHERE chosen by the bridge, the plan still genuinely produced by solve(), the executed steps still equal to it, every gate green. place asserts (obj_at_boxel ?o ?b) as an effect, so the conjunct is plannable. This is the archived failure (boxel_policy.py:68-105 hand-built the problem so that exactly one plan existed) re-entering through the one new input channel v4 opens. The same gap exists for target_name (nothing asserts its category equals task_spec's target category) and for main()'s disposal goal.
findings.evidence: pddl/domain_pddlstream.pddl:295-304 (place effect obj_at_boxel); test_full_pipeline.py:762 (today's goal built inside main), :1323-1325 (goal passed verbatim to planner.plan), :1380-1383 (disposal goal ('handempty',)); pddlstream_planner.py:206-221 (plan takes goal as given); plan_v4.txt:179-196, 800-816.
findings.required_change: Add to G10, unconditional at every plan() call: the goal argument equals exactly ('and', ('holding', T), ('at_config', q_home)) for mission plans, or exactly ('handempty',) for main()'s disposal plan, where T is the symbol whose category (from the identity table) equals task_spec's target category and planner_target_objects == [T]; write the goal into the ledger per plan id; count a mismatch in G21. State in B3(c) that goal is built by one function from task_spec fields with its own test, not by free bridge code. Add a B0 positive-control test in which an extra obj_at_boxel conjunct must trip the gate.

findings.title: B7's GUI episodes must be gate-green, but the GUI overlay creates, repositions and removes bodies on the executing client, which G14 and G1 forbid
findings.plan_location: P4.1 G1 and G14 (:81-94, 214-232); P4.4 B7 GO criterion (:897-908) and the B2 GUI twin (:778-783); R3.8 additions
findings.problem: B7 runs seed 0 and seed 1 with the GUI and requires G1-G21 green with no gate trip in any of the four episodes. In GUI mode main() builds BoxelVisualizer when gui and draw_boxel_overlays are true (default True). BoxelVisualizer._draw_boxel_phantom calls createVisualShape and createMultiBody on the default client, which in the bridge is their executing client; remove_boxel_viz calls removeBody; every perception render is bracketed by conceal_overlay_for_observation and restore_overlay_after_observation, which resetBasePositionAndOrientation every phantom 100 m down and back. v4's R3.8 made createMultiBody and loadURDF fail outright on the executing client and put removeBody and resetBasePositionAndOrientation into the G1 grep. Every GUI episode therefore trips G14 and G21 at its first overlay draw, and visualization.py:66, 83, 176, 254, 327, 344 are G1 hits with no allowlist entry. Nothing in the plan says whether the bridge's GUI runs disable the overlay.
findings.evidence: visualization.py:58-86 (conceal/restore teleports), :168-185 (createVisualShape, createMultiBody, no client argument), :254, :327, :344 (removeBody); test_full_pipeline.py:652-656 (viz built when gui and draw_boxel_overlays), :455 and :2540 (draw_boxel_overlays kwarg); boxel_env.py:22, :581; plan_v4.txt:214-232, 897-908.
findings.required_change: Pre-register one of: (a) every bridge GUI run passes draw_boxel_overlays=False (the kwarg exists), stated in B2's GUI twin and in B7; or (b) a G1 and G14 exemption for BoxelVisualizer's overlay bodies (visual-only, mass 0, no collision shape), listed by file:line with a BF#, asserted to touch only bodies created by BoxelVisualizer, with the conceal/restore render bracket named as the only teleport and G20 accepting the GUI pane render. Option (a) is the smaller change.

findings.title: main() ends with env.close(), which disconnects the adopted executing client before D3 and G6 read it
findings.problem: main() always finishes with env.close() (and also calls it on early-exit paths), and BoxelTestEnv.close() calls p.disconnect on self.client_id and self.plan_client_id. Under B3(b)'s adopt-client path self.client_id is their executing client 0. After main() returns, execute_fn must read the 7 arm joints and the pad contacts (D3) and G6 requires the readback to be logged 'at main() return'; both hit a disconnected client. The constructor's failure path also calls close() (boxel_env.py:541-545). B2 states the adapter overrides nothing except two oracle methods, and B3(b) specifies no lifecycle behaviour, so the plan as written cannot produce the scoring observation. In GUI runs main() additionally steps the executing client for 4 s after its last action (test_full_pipeline.py:2353-2358), which settles the arm toward its last motor targets inside main() and is invisible to G6's outside-main() step count, so a scored GUI state is not comparable with a headless one.
findings.evidence: test_full_pipeline.py:2362 (env.close()), :760, :794, :807; boxel_env.py:1898-1907 (close disconnects client_id and plan_client_id), :541-545; plan_v4.txt:139-150, 439-455, 792-799.
findings.required_change: B3(b): the adopt path owns only the plan twin, so close() disconnects the plan twin and never the adopted client (also in the constructor failure path); add a B3 test that the adopted client id is still connected after main() returns; list this override among the adapter's permitted overrides in B2. State that scored episodes are headless only (GUI runs are not scored), so the 4 s GUI loop never feeds D3.

findings.title: M1 changes sense to three parameters but the executor unpacks exactly two, and B4 lists no executor change
findings.problem: M1 makes sense take (?o ?region ?q), so the dispatched plan tuple is ('sense', o, region, q). The dispatcher passes action[1:] to handle_sense_action, whose first statement is 'obj, shadow_id = action_params', a two-value unpack. The first sense of any M1 episode raises ValueError. B4 is described as the only domain change with the deliverable 'G3 shows no other difference' and Abort 'any precondition removal'; it names no executor edit, and B3's default-off acceptance does not cover it. Since adoption of M1 is the expected outcome, B4 would force an unregistered main-pipeline edit in the middle of the schedule.
findings.evidence: execution.py:2460 ('obj, shadow_id = action_params'); test_full_pipeline.py:1611-1621 (sense dispatch passes params); pddl/domain_pddlstream.pddl:169-191 (current two-parameter sense); plan_v4.txt:843-855, 951-958.
findings.required_change: B4 (or B3 as a refactor) registers the executor change: handle_sense_action accepts the extra clearance parameter (default-neutral for the two-parameter form), plus any other consumer of the sense tuple (ledger comparison of identical args, world_eye labels); B4's deliverable is an executed sense on the clearance scene, not only a plan that contains the move.

findings.title: GATE-FAILED EPISODES is defined only through G21 counters, so several gates have no per-episode outcome
findings.plan_location: P4.1 G21 (:267-271) and G4, G13, G15, G18, G19; P4.6 SUCCESS and HARNESS STOP RULE (:1149-1155); B8 abort (:916-918); P4.9 R17
findings.problem: R3.14's fix says an episode with any G21 count above 0 counts as a failure of its arm, keeps its row and is flagged. G21's list is the runtime hooks of G3, G5, G6 (stepSimulation outside main()), G8, G10, G11, G14, G16 and G20. G4 (place destination fidelity) and G15 (sense fidelity) are ledger checks, G18 (clock) is proved from ledger timestamps, G19 (scene file equals the pinned map, seed hygiene) is an assertion, G13 (tree and pip-freeze hash) is per run, G12 is a reporting rule. None increments a G21 counter, so a violation of any of them during B8 has no pre-registered outcome (fail the arm, drop, stop, or abort), and the decision would be taken after seeing which arm and seed tripped, which is exactly R17. B7's GO criterion says 'G1-G21 green' but B8 and P4.6 only cover G21.
findings.required_change: Make every per-episode gate produce a ledger boolean or counter that P4.6 treats like a G21 count (episode counts as a failure of its arm, row kept and flagged with the gate name), and name the outcome of the per-run gates: a G13 hash or freeze change, or a G19 scene-map mismatch, stops the campaign with the partial table reported and a new campaign for the rerun. Rename or extend G21 accordingly and list the same set in B8's abort conditions.

findings.title: B2's 'no planning yet' deliverable needs a stop point that none of the six pre-registered main() keywords provides
findings.plan_location: P4.4 B2 deliverable (:771-777) and B3(c) keyword list (:800-816); P4.10 Q6 ('six keyword arguments')
findings.problem: B2 must show, on seeds 0 and 1, D9, main()'s own settle, OBJECT and lateral boxels from the first render and plan-twin poses equal to registry centres, 'no planning yet'. The plan-twin sync that makes those poses checkable happens at test_full_pipeline.py:998, after the planner is constructed, and the loop then calls planner.plan() at :1323. main() has no early-exit parameter; B3(c)'s after_settle runs before Phase 2, not after Phase 3. Either main() runs to completion in B2 (contradicting 'no planning yet' and exercising G3, G10, G11, G5 outside B2's gate list) or an implementer adds a stop hook or a seventh keyword, an unregistered main-pipeline change outside Q6's 'six'.
findings.evidence: test_full_pipeline.py:454-464 (main signature, no stop parameter), :610-650 (Phase 2 and 3), :952-958 (planner built), :998 (first sync), :1209-1323 (loop and first plan call); plan_v4.txt:771-777, 800-816, 1339-1342.
findings.required_change: Pick one and register it: add a stop keyword (for example stop_before_planning, default off) to B3(c) and Q6 under the B3 acceptance, or restate B2's deliverable as a probe that drives the same env methods (settle, get_camera_observation, generate_free_space, registry build, sync) inside execute_fn without main(), with main() end to end first exercised in B7.

findings.title: D7(vii)'s final hold has no pre-registered criterion or step cap, and the ordering (B3 implements, B1(i) measures) leaves the number to be chosen later
findings.problem: D7(vii) says a move to q_home ends with a final hold that 'converges to their tolerance or a bounded step cap (an executor mode, default off)'. The cap value, the convergence test and the gain are not stated. B3(d) implements the mode, B3's acceptance closes before B1 part 2, and B1(i) then measures 'steps under the D7 final hold'; no sentence says how that measurement fixes the cap, who freezes it, or what happens if the held arm cannot reach 1e-4 within any sensible cap (D11 has a user-decision branch for the analogous grasp case, D7 has none). The cap decides whether the at-home conjunct can ever pass, so it is the one number that governs the headline's strict test, and R7 calls home_not_reached 'the one new bound' while this is a second. Choosing it after B1(i) or after B7 episodes is the outcome fitting R8 forbids.
findings.evidence: robot_utils.py:777-788 (today's endpoint hold: 120-step cap, 2e-3 tolerance, hard-coded); plan_v4.txt:575-577, 738-741, 817-824, 1276-1280, 1293-1299.
findings.required_change: Pre-register in D7(vii): the convergence test is their allclose on the 7-joint readback; the cap is a task_spec constant set once from B1(i)'s empty-table worst case (state the margin rule, for example twice the maximum steps over the empty-handed and payload probes) and frozen in B6; the executor mode reads it, so B3 needs no number; add B1(i)'s outcome branch (if 1e-4 is not reached within the cap with payload, the user decides before B7); list the cap beside home_not_reached in R7.

findings.title: W is defined as a set of cells, but no package says how it reaches the rectangular workspace parameters of free space and shadow casting
findings.problem: D8 defines W as their shortened-table region intersected with the reach envelope, keeping only cells whose whole column projects into the D4 frame and is free of robot pixels, and says it applies to free space, placement candidates and ShadowCalculator; D6's status rule queries 'free cells inside W' as a record. Free-space generation and shadow casting take only axis-aligned x and y ranges (FreeSpaceGenerator and ShadowCalculator constructors), and the planner's placement cells come from the free-space boxels. B3's parameter list has no workspace parameter beyond the pick floor and reach constants, B2 only 'declares' W, B6 only 'freezes' it. How a non-rectangular cell set becomes the rectangle (bounding box, largest inscribed rectangle) or a new mask feature is an unregistered decision that changes where O may place objects, and a choice made after seeing placements near the boundary would be outcome fitting.
findings.evidence: free_space.py:27-29, 47-48 (rectangular table_x_range, table_y_range); boxel_env.py:548-567 (ShadowCalculator, FreeSpaceGenerator, UniformGridGenerator built from the ranges); pddlstream_planner.py:866-882 (placement cells from free-space boxels); plan_v4.txt:597-606, 521-536, 759, 766-768.
findings.required_change: State W's representation and the consuming mechanism in B3(b) or B2: either W is an axis-aligned rectangle derived once in B6 by a stated rule (for example the largest inscribed rectangle of the cell set) and passed as the existing table ranges, with D6's record queried against the same rectangle; or a cell-mask feature is added to B3 (default off) with the A/B. Name the package that implements it.
